scope: Accumulated independent source records published first; this audit is being extended only for landform confirmations 049-064 and environment confirmations 145-160. Source-status claims are conservative and do not accept the benchmark.

venus.supported_facts_paraphrase: Rotation takes longer than orbit; dense atmosphere mainly carbon dioxide; sulfuric-acid clouds; retrograde rotation.

uranus.supported_facts_paraphrase: Near-sideways axial tilt; rings discovered in 1977; ice-giant classification.

neptune.supported_facts_paraphrase: Fast winds; Voyager 2 visit in 1989; Great Dark Spot; atmospheric methane.

pluto.supported_facts_paraphrase: Charon largest moon; Kuiper Belt location; New Horizons visit in 2015; heart-shaped Tombaugh Regio.

ceres.supported_facts_paraphrase: Largest asteroid-belt object; Occator bright salts; Dawn mission.

titan.supported_facts_paraphrase: Largest Saturnian moon; hydrocarbon lakes; Huygens landing in 2005.

europa.supported_facts_paraphrase: Smallest Galilean moon; inferred liquid-water ocean; water-ice crust.

io.supported_facts_paraphrase: Innermost Galilean moon; strong volcanic activity.

helium.supported_facts_paraphrase: Helium: atomic number 2; nonflammable balloon gas; noble gas.

lithium.supported_facts_paraphrase: Lithium: atomic number 3; symbol Li; lightest metal; rechargeable batteries.

boron.supported_facts_paraphrase: Boron: atomic number 5; metalloid; oxide used in borosilicate glass.

cobalt.supported_facts_paraphrase: Cobalt: atomic number 27; symbol Co; vitamin B12; blue pigment; German kobold etymology.

nickel.supported_facts_paraphrase: Nickel: atomic number 28; symbol Ni; US five-cent coin.

tungsten.supported_facts_paraphrase: Tungsten: atomic number 74; symbol W; highest metal melting point; lamp filaments.

radon.supported_facts_paraphrase: Radon: atomic number 86; symbol Rn; radioactive gas from radium decay; indoor accumulation.

neon.supported_facts_paraphrase: Neon: atomic number 10; symbol Ne; orange-red discharge.

cellchem.supported_facts_paraphrase: DNA/RNA structures, sugars and base pairing; insulin chains; hemoglobin four globin chains and heme.

neurons.supported_facts_paraphrase: Neurons: axons, dendrites, synapses and myelin.

nucleus.supported_facts_paraphrase: Nucleus encloses chromosomes in a membrane.

insulin.supported_facts_paraphrase: Insulin from beta cells in pancreatic islets lowers blood glucose.

hemoglobin.supported_facts_paraphrase: Red blood cells contain oxygen-carrying iron-rich hemoglobin.

chlorophyll.supported_facts_paraphrase: Magnesium occupies the central position in chlorophyll, the green plant pigment.

collagen.supported_facts_paraphrase: Collagen gives structural strength to tendons; three chains form a triple helix; glycine occurs every third residue.

danube.supported_facts_paraphrase: Danube drains into the Black Sea.

danube_history.supported_facts_paraphrase: Danube begins in the Black Forest, passes four national capitals, and reaches the Black Sea.

mekong.supported_facts_paraphrase: Mekong rises on the Tibetan Plateau and passes through six countries.

borneo.supported_facts_paraphrase: Kinabalu Park is in Sabah, Malaysia, on Borneo.

einstein.supported_facts_paraphrase: Einstein born in Ulm; 1921 Physics Nobel for photoelectric effect, received in 1922.

gutenberg.supported_facts_paraphrase: Gutenberg printed Latin Vulgate in Mainz using movable metal type; forty-two-line Bible.

confucius.supported_facts_paraphrase: Confucius lived in ancient China, traditionally 551–479 BCE; teachings associated with Analects.

shakespeare.supported_facts_paraphrase: Shakespeare born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564; playwright.

beethoven.supported_facts_paraphrase: Beethoven born in Bonn; died in Vienna.

beethoven_works.supported_facts_paraphrase: Beethoven chronology attributes Fidelio and Ninth Symphony and records Vienna death.

mozart.supported_facts_paraphrase: Mozart born in 1756; Salzburg family residence; Don Giovanni attribution.

picasso_guernica.supported_facts_paraphrase: Guernica painted by Pablo Picasso in 1937.

picasso_demoiselles.supported_facts_paraphrase: Les Demoiselles d’Avignon is a 1907 Picasso work.

monet.supported_facts_paraphrase: Monet: Impression, Sunrise and Impressionism; Water Lilies and garden at Giverny.

linux.supported_facts_paraphrase: Linux is a Unix-like kernel written by Linus Torvalds.

linux_license.supported_facts_paraphrase: Linux kernel uses GNU GPL version 2; FAQ discusses Tux logo.

python.supported_facts_paraphrase: Guido van Rossum created Python and publicly posted it in February 1991; PEP means Python Enhancement Proposal; name comes from BBC comedy series Monty Python’s Flying Circus.

voyager.supported_facts_paraphrase: Voyager pair launched in 1977; Voyager 1 reached interstellar boundary in 2012; both spacecraft carry Golden Records.

hubble.supported_facts_paraphrase: Hubble deployed by Discovery in 1990; low Earth orbit; 2.4-metre primary mirror.

unicode.supported_facts_paraphrase: Unicode first version dates to 1991; code points use U+ notation; UTF-8 uses at most four bytes.

ethernet_origin.supported_facts_paraphrase: Bob Metcalfe proposed Ethernet on May 22, 1973 at Xerox.

ethernet.supported_facts_paraphrase: Experimental Ethernet developed at PARC; later 10Mb Ethernet uses 48-bit host addresses.

si.supported_facts_paraphrase: SI tables bind kelvin K/temperature/Boltzmann constant; pascal Pa/N per square metre/pressure; newton N/kg m s^-2/force; watt W/J per second/power; tesla T/Wb per square metre/flux density; volt V/potential difference; mole mol/amount of substance/Avogadro constant; gray Gy/absorbed dose.

ozone.supported_facts_paraphrase: Ozone O3 contains three oxygen atoms; stratospheric ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation.

monsoon.supported_facts_paraphrase: Monsoon is seasonal wind shift, associated with wet summers and dry winters; Arabic mausim means season.

permafrost.supported_facts_paraphrase: Permafrost remains frozen at least two years; active layer thaws seasonally; thawed organic matter releases carbon dioxide and methane.

active_layer.supported_facts_paraphrase: Active layer undergoes annual thawing and freezing.

env_noaa_ozone.claim: Most ozone resides in the stratosphere; stratospheric ozone absorbs biologically damaging UV-B; ozone molecules consist of three oxygen atoms and have formula O3.

env_unesco_causeway.claim: The Giant’s Causeway exposes about 40,000 polygonal basalt columns; its geology records lava flows and columnar basalt lavas.

env_nps_igneous.claim: NPS defines intrusive rocks as solidifying within Earth and extrusive rocks as erupted at the surface; its classification table places basalt among extrusive mafic rocks and granite among intrusive rocks; granite is predominantly quartz and feldspar with biotite/muscovite.

env_nps_volcanic.claim: Magma at spreading centers is mafic, and much oceanic crust is basalt, a mafic rock.

env_nps_rushmore.claim: Mount Rushmore contains granite; molten rock cooled underground to form the granite, and a block of fine-grained granite forms the upper portion of Mount Rushmore.

env_govscot_rubislaw.claim: The Aberdeen granite age is tied to samples from the Rubislaw quarry; the Aberdeen pluton is grey muscovite-biotite granite, with abundant quartz, feldspar, and mica, and the report identifies Rubislaw quarries as a principal location.

env_noaa_monsoon.publisher: NOAA National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information Service
env_noaa_monsoon.claim: NOAA describes a monsoon as a seasonal wind shift; monsoons causing the heaviest rainfall are summer monsoons near the Indian Ocean, while winter monsoons there are usually dry; the word monsoon comes from Arabic mausim.

env_usgs_glacier.claim: USGS defines a glacier as a large perennial accumulation that moves downslope under its own weight and gravity.

env_nps_glacial_geology.publisher: U.S. National Park Service, Glacier National Park
env_nps_glacial_geology.claim: NPS describes glaciers as masses of ice moving under gravity, explains that glaciers scour valleys into U-shapes, and identifies the debris ridge deposited at a glacier terminus as a moraine.

env_nws_efscale.publisher: NOAA National Weather Service, Norman Weather Forecast Office
env_nws_efscale.claim: The Enhanced Fujita (EF) Scale assigns tornado ratings from EF0 to EF5 using surveyed damage and estimated wind speeds; NWS provides the official ratings.

env_nws_tornado_glossary.claim: The NWS glossary defines a tornado as a violently rotating column of air usually pendant to a cumulonimbus, with circulation reaching the ground.

env_usgs_earthquake_facts.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Hazards Program
env_usgs_earthquake_facts.claim: USGS states that an earthquake hypocenter is beneath the surface where fault rupture begins and the epicenter is directly above it at the surface.

env_usgs_richter.claim: USGS describes the Richter scale as a logarithmic earthquake magnitude scale developed by Charles Richter; it also explains that moment magnitude was developed as a more broadly applicable replacement.

env_nsidc_permafrost.publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center
env_nsidc_permafrost.claim: NSIDC defines permafrost as ground at or below 0°C for at least two years, identifies the annually freezing/thawing active layer, and states that thawing permafrost organic matter decays and releases carbon dioxide and/or methane.

env_nsidc_active_layer.publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center
env_nsidc_active_layer.claim: NSIDC defines the active layer as ground subject to annual thawing and freezing over permafrost.

env_noaa_chlorine_depletion.supported_facts_paraphrase: Cl and ClO participate in chain reactions destroying stratospheric ozone.
